solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Behold one's girl

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
one is the Roman numeral I, plus the apostrophe-s

explanation.surface: An exclamation drawing attention to someone's girlfriend or daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lois is a female first name, and crosswords freely clue any given name by the word girl.

clue.text: Hum nothing gloomy

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
dour means stern and gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone humming a tune without any cheerfulness in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum is not the musical sound here: in British slang it is a bad smell, as in 'what a hum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hum is informal British for a smell, usually an unpleasant one, which is an odour.

clue.text: Very disappointed not to be quite qualifying for Python sketch?

definitions.text: not to be quite qualifying for Python sketch

blocks.note: first meaning: a British idiom, famously used by footballers after a defeat

blocks.clueFragment: not to be quite qualifying for Python sketch
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: Monty Python's Dead Parrot sketch needed a bird in a worse state than merely unwell

explanation.surface: A comedian dismayed that a routine falls short of being worthy of Monty Python.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Monty Python sketch the parrot is dead, not merely ill, so a parrot that was only poorly would not quite qualify for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means bitterly let down, a cliché of post-match football interviews.

clue.text: Football club employing round ball is concentrating

indicators.note: round means going around, so the outer letters are placed either side of the ball

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in Chelsea FC
employing something is using it
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A football club deploying a round ball, keen on its tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round ball' reads as one phrase, but round is the container signal and ball alone is the piece that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Focusing on something means directing all attention to it, which is concentrating.

clue.text: Impose fine on illegal street trader first of all

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following words is taken, not just one

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A penalty slapped on an unlicensed pavement vendor.
explanation.definitionFit: To foist something on someone is to force it upon them unwelcome, to impose it.

clue.text: Cooks in less than boiling water, and spoils

definitions.text: Cooks in less than boiling water

blocks.clueFragment: Cooks in less than boiling water
blocks.note: first meaning: gently poaching, as with eggs
second meaning: pampers or overprotects

explanation.surface: A cook who simmers food gently and ruins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coddling eggs means cooking them just below the boil; coddling a child means overindulging it.

clue.text: Pi to be worked out: so sum in action!

indicators.note: working out a puzzle means rearranging its parts until they fit

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A maths teacher urging pupils to calculate pi with a working sum.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi is not the number but the British slang short form of pious, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Pi is slang for pious in a smug way, which is what sanctimonious means: making a show of virtue.

clue.text: Recently arrived in Spain, Rob went climbing

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
in a down clue climbing means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the end of Spain, all of Rob and most of went

explanation.surface: A traveller who has just landed in Spain where someone called Rob went hiking.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby is one that has only just arrived in the world.

clue.text: Sponsored youngster did clog dancing outside hotel

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and land in a new order
the rearranged letters stand outside, wrapping round the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A child whose dance lessons were paid for performed a clog dance outside a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A godchild has godparents who sponsor them at baptism, promising to oversee their upbringing.

clue.text: Amphibian that we notice partially retreating

indicators.note: partially says only part of the words that follow is used
retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the end of that, all of we and the start of notice

explanation.surface: A frog or toad we spot backing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small tailed amphibian related to salamanders.

clue.text: What kids never play at school

definitions.text: What kids never play at school

blocks.clueFragment: What kids never play at school
blocks.note: surface reading: a game banned in the playground
setter's reading: the role you play when you skip lessons, and someone playing it is by definition not at school

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is to play the absent pupil; anyone doing it is away from school, so they can never do it there.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil who stays away from school without permission; 'playing' one is the fixed idiom.

clue.text: Little piggy from the west?

blocks.note: coming from the west means heading to the east: TO plus E

explanation.surface: A small pig that has come from the western counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Something travelling from the west is going TO the E(ast); the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market', each piggy is one of a child's toes.

clue.text: Draws group — to scale, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a lot is a group or batch
taken as written
first letter of scale

explanation.surface: A set of pictures drawn to scale.
explanation.walkthrough: Draws looks like a verb for sketching, which the surface supports; it is a plural noun for prize draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Lottos are lottery games, draws in which numbered tickets win prizes.

clue.text: Smelt absinthe being distilled in business premises

indicators.note: distilling transforms a liquid, so the letters are processed into a new form

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone noticing the smell of absinthe being made at a distillery.
explanation.walkthrough: Smelt looks like a past tense of smell or a metalworking verb, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment is a place of business such as a shop, hotel or restaurant.

clue.text: Preparation for locks is fake, low-quality, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
poor means of low quality

explanation.surface: A cheap counterfeit lock-oiling product for doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks suggests doors and keys; here they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid preparation for washing hair, and locks are tresses of hair.

clue.text: Pasta dish ruined alas and starter of guacamole not available

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper order
a starter is the first course, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
first letter of guacamole
N/A is the standard abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A diner laments a spoilt meal with no guacamole to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is baked pasta in flat sheets layered with sauce, an Italian dish.

clue.text: Restrict clothing for male couple

blocks.note: first meaning: to bind or limit
second meaning: a neckwear item worn by men
a third meaning: to join or link together

explanation.surface: A dress code limiting what a man in a couple may wear.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really three meanings strung together: restrict, a man's neckwear, and couple, which is to join.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie restricts movement, is worn knotted at a man's collar, and ties also connect things.

clue.text: Has to contain brief rash causing bother

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so one word wraps the other
brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
rash with its tail removed

explanation.surface: Someone who has a quick-spreading rash that is troubling them.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass someone is to pester or torment them, the verb sense of bother.

clue.text: Is capable, then led astray? That's wicked!

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off the right path, so the letters stray out of order

blocks.note: someone who is capable can
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A competent person who was misled into sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Wicked sounds like evil, which fits the surface's moral tone; read literally it means having a wick.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle is a thing with a wick, so it is literally wicked, a pun on the word for evil.

clue.text: Joyous song Lorca composed

indicators.note: composing means putting parts together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A happy song written by the Spanish poet Federico García Lorca.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a joyful hymn, especially one sung at Christmas.

clue.text: Lounges with sweets: ie has gone missing!

indicators.note: something gone missing is no longer there, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: lollies are lollipops, sweets on a stick
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Someone slumped on a sofa discovering the sweet stash has vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or sprawl lazily, so lolls is the matching verb form of lounges.

clue.text: Pole to fight, but not seriously

blocks.note: first meaning: a stout pole used on a ship as a mast or boom
second meaning: to box in practice

explanation.surface: A Polish person spoiling for a scrap that is only for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a nationality because of the capital letter, which is just the first word of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a sturdy pole in a ship's rigging, and to spar is to box for practice.

clue.text: Olga Grey is up the spout

definitions.note: the article goes with the noun; a gargoyle is a spout

indicators.note: up can mean amiss, as in 'what's up?', so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman named Olga Grey is pregnant, 'up the spout' being British slang for that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the spout' reads as one idiom (ruined or pregnant), but splits so that the spout is the definition. Olga Grey was a silent-film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque on a roof that works as a waterspout, carrying rain clear of the wall.

clue.text: Game: it follows daily dance

blocks.note: so means therefore, as in 'it follows that'
the Financial Times, a daily newspaper
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A game played after a regular dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a newspaper; the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Softball is a game similar to baseball, played with a larger ball pitched underarm.

clue.text: Hard to follow some elite military band

blocks.note: the SAS is the British Army's elite Special Air Service regiment
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough musical group following a crack army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Band looks musical, which the military setting supports; it is a strip of cloth worn across the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a broad band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.
